text:
Tye Kartye played 180 games for Seattle and Eeli Tolvanen 288, and tonight both walk back into that building in Rangers colours for the first time. Kartye's story is the better one this month. The New York Post's headline says he is "making every minute count with Rangers after he was claimed off waivers," and our numbers flag him as a breakout: more ice, more chances.

The Rangers are getting by without Igor Shesterkin, and that's the sentence that frames their season so far. Dylan Garand has carried it: 13 games, .906, 2.2 goals saved above expected. New York lost three straight either side of Halloween, then beat St. Louis and Philadelphia with 63% and 57% of the expected goals. Sean Durzi is out too; Braden Schneider has moved up beside Pettersson and Adam Fox is playing 24:17 a night. Our Sleeper here is Pavel Dorofeyev, a third-liner whose shots have been dangerous: 4.8 expected goals in his last ten games, better per 60 minutes than 99% of depth forwards. We have him at 31% to score.

Seattle is a puzzle. The Kraken have 19 points, the same as New York, but their chances say they should have about 14. They're at 45% of the expected goals at five on five and scoring 3.47 a game anyway. Jared McCann is out until January; Jordan Eberle has taken his spot beside Matty Beniers and Mackie Samoskevich, and Beniers, who won Wednesday's game against Calgary in overtime, is on the top power play. Berkly Catton, the eighth pick in 2024, has points in seven straight.

The worry is in net. Philipp Grubauer is at .863 and 5.5 goals worse than expected over his last five starts. Our numbers like New York, 3.21 expected goals to 2.85, and give the Rangers a 48% playoff chance against Seattle's 41%. If the Kraken's finishing cools before Grubauer warms up, this could get away from them.
headline: Two old Kraken come back to Seattle

hunch.text: Old buildings, old teammates, a player on waivers a few weeks ago who keeps getting chances. Our hunch: Tye Kartye scores in his first game back in Seattle.
